title: Emissions: world has four times the work or one-third of the time
problem: The paper focuses on the widening "emissions gap" between insufficient national climate pledges and the rapid, deep emission cuts required to meet Paris Agreement targets, a challenge severely exacerbated by a decade of political inaction.
method: This paper proposes an approach for closing the climate emissions gap through immediate, crisis-level action, where governments, businesses, and communities make more ambitious pledges and implement rapid, transformative changes.
task: The task is to synthesize a decade of reports to quantify the growing gap between the emissions cuts required to meet Paris Agreement goals and the insufficient climate pledges and actions made by countries.
innovation: This paper synthesizes a decade of UNEP Emissions Gap Reports to demonstrate that political inaction has shrunk the time available to halve global emissions from 30 to 10 years, drastically increasing the required annual rate of reduction to meet the goals of the Paris Agreement.

The tenth anniversary of the report coincides with the 2020 milestone to which countries agreed in Paris. They undertook to communicate or update climate pledges, or 'nationally determined contributions', to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change conference (COP26) this November in Glasgow, UK. Clearly, the promises must be overhauled — and then, crucially, kept — if the yawning gap between 'talk and walk' is going to close by 2030.
